jobs.title: Environmental Program Manager
jobs.description:
About Us

We are Sila, a next-generation battery materials company. Our mission is to power the world’s transition to clean energy. To create this future, our team is building a better lithium-ion battery from the inside out today. We engineer and manufacture ground-breaking battery materials that significantly increase the energy density of batteries, while reducing their size and weight. The result? Smaller more powerful batteries that can unlock innovation in consumer devices and accelerate the mass adoption of electric cars to eliminate our dependence on fossil fuels. We're tackling one of the biggest challenges of our time every day, and together we're redefining what's possible. Are you ready to be a part of a team committed to changing the world?

Who You Are

The Corporate EHS&S Program Manager is a high-level leader responsible for working cross-functionally to steward the strategic direction, implementation, and health of Sila’s company-wide Environmental, Health, Safety, and Sustainability programs. Operating at the corporate level, this role does not manage day-to-day site operations; instead, you will architect the overarching EHS&S Management Systems, governance models, and compliance frameworks that enable Sila to safely develop and scale its technology across R&D and high-volume manufacturing.

As a master cross-functional orchestrator and executive communicator, you will lead through influence, partnering with EHS&S site managers, R&D, engineering, and operations to maintain a rigorous culture of safety, health, and environmental stewardship into our commercial execution as we scale manufacturing of batteries and battery materials in the US.

Responsibilities and Duties

- Enterprise EHS&S Governance: Architect, implement, and continuously improve corporate EHS&S Management Systems. Partner with site teams to define the global standards, policies, and continuous improvement frameworks (e.g., environmental permitting & compliance, LOTO, Hazard Recognition, Compliance), and ensure they are executed across all sites.

- Prioritization & Scale-Up: Partner with Operations, R&D, and Process Safety to prioritize, sequence, and de-risk EHS&S workstreams required for technology transfer and manufacturing scale-up. Identify and bridge cross-functional gaps before they impact commercial timelines.

- Metrics & Single Source of Truth: Design and maintain centralized enterprise databases, KPIs, and governance tools to ensure EHS&S metrics, compliance data, and goals are synchronized across the organization.

- Executive Communication & Risk Management: Act as the central point of accountability for enterprise EHS&S program health. Distill complex technical and regulatory risks into crisp briefings for executive leadership, proactively facilitating mitigation strategies for cross-program roadblocks.

- Cross-Functional Decision Facilitation: Lead steering committees composed of EHS&S site leads, Process Safety representatives, engineering, and other personnel to drive alignment on high-stakes EHS investments, corporate roadmaps, and risk prioritization.

Knowledge and Skill Requirements

- Industry Experience: 10+ years of professional experience building and scaling corporate EHS&S programs within heavy tech, chemicals, automotive, or advanced manufacturing industries.

- Scale-Up Expertise: Minimum 5 years leading large-scale technical programs, with demonstrated experience supporting technology transfer from R&D into high-volume commercial manufacturing environments.

- Education: Bachelor’s degree or higher in EHS, Environmental Science, Chemical Engineering, or a related engineering/technical discipline. Certified Safety Professional (CSP) or Certified Industrial Hygienist (CIH) preferred.

Physical Demands and Working Conditions

- Work onsite in either Alameda or Moses Lake and travel frequently to the other location (~ 25%).

- Wear personal protective equipment including, but not limited to, a respirator, a lab coat, gloves, safety glasses, head protection, flame resistant clothing, and safety shoes.

- Move long distances (such as from building to building) and be stationary for extended periods of time.

- Operate a computer and other office equipment, such as a laptop, copier/printer, etc in a fixed location.

The starting base pay for this role is between $159,000 and $201,000 at the time of posting. The actual base pay depends on many factors, such as education, experience, and skills. Base pay is only one part of Sila’s competitive Total Rewards package that can include benefits, perks, and equity.  The base pay range is subject to change and may be modified in the future.

Who You Are

Sila’s Program Managers act as the "flight control tower" for our critical, multi-year integrated programs. This leadership role bridges R&D, engineering, capital project, and commercial workstreams to ensure complex products scale smoothly from lab to market. You aren't executing the functional tasks—you are orchestrating the sequencing, integration, and high-stakes decision-making required to land our strategic objectives safely, on time, and in-line with target financial metrics.

Responsibilities and Duties

- Integrated Leadership: Drive major cross-functional programs linking R&D (materials/equipment/battery development), Operations (manufacturing), Capital Projects (manufacturing scale-up), and Product + Commercial teams (customer "Plans to Win").

- Workflow Architect: Design and communicate workflows to resolve complex uncertainties and decisions. Maintain the "single source of truth" (integrated databases and governance tools) to keep objectives, metrics, and technical data synchronized across functions.

- Execution & Sequencing: Optimize the timing of R&D breakthroughs, scale-up projects, and commercial milestones to hit financial and strategic targets (e.g., revenue run rate, ROIC).

- Executive Communication & Partnership: Serve as the central point of accountability for program health, working closely with the Exec Sponsor and Steering Team to steward the program’s direction and approach. Deliver crisp status updates, risk assessments, and roadblock resolutions to executives and collaborators. Lead and participate in company-wide, cross-program prioritization efforts.

- Decision & Risk Management: Lead execs and functional managers through high-stakes decisions (e.g., project scoping, partner selection) and proactively mitigate cross-program dependencies before they impact timelines.

Knowledge and Skill Requirements

-

- Industry Experience: 10+ years in battery technology, automotive, chemical process, semiconductor, oil & gas, or a similarly complex hardware-plus-process industry.

- Program Leadership: 5+ years leading complex technical and/or business programs that integrate R&D, manufacturing scale-up, and commercial execution.

- Scale-up Expertise: Proven experience transferring novel technology and/or products from R&D into high-volume manufacturing environments.

- Education: Bachelor’s degree or higher in an Engineering or Physical Science field.

- Program Management Fundamentals SME: Deep, demonstrable expertise in core program and project management disciplines—including decision quality, scheduling, budgeting, project framing, financial analysis, risk communication and analysis, and resource allocation.

- Systemic Program Architect: Proven ability to navigate a matrix model, ensuring functional activities support macro program objectives without duplicating effort.

- Master Communicator: Skilled at distilling complex technical, financial, and commercial data into clear, actionable insights for diverse audiences.

- Strategic Influence: Adept at driving alignment among executives and SMEs, escalating effectively, and balancing technical risks with business objectives.

- New Product Introduction & Tech Transfer Mastery: Strong understanding of Stage-Gate methodologies, with the ability to leverage Agile or Waterfall frameworks depending on the workflow.

- Ambiguity Management: Comfortable driving execution and maintaining momentum especially in the face of uncertainties, when strategies shift, or deliverables are fluid.

Physical Demands and Working Conditions

- Ability to wear personal protective equipment (PPE) including safety glasses, lab coats, and steel-toe shoes when visiting laboratory or manufacturing environments.

- Ability to work at a computer for extended periods.

Responsibilities and Duties

Strategic NPI & Partner Management

- Lead end-to-end NPI execution, driving qualification for new suppliers and external manufacturing partners (OEMs).

Product Risk Management & Quality Engineering

- Own core NPI documentation, including Engineering Bills of Materials (BOMs), design specifications, and partner Statements of Work (SOWs).

- Process Knowledge: Practical understanding of cell manufacturing processes, risk analysis (FMEA), and global safety/certification frameworks.

Key Competencies

- Cross-Functional Leadership: Proven ability to align diverse engineering, operations, and commercial teams around high-velocity timelines.

Preferred Qualifications

- Fluency in Mandarin, Korean, or Japanese (to support Asian manufacturing partner interfaces).

Who You Are

The Director of Strategic Planning will design, scale, and lead the overarching demand, production, and supply chain planning ecosystem for Sila’s next-generation battery materials. Sitting at the intersection of Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Sales, Strategy, and Finance, you will architect business processes, advanced systems, and executive reporting to drive organizational alignment. You will own and elevate the Sales, Inventory, and Operations Planning (SIOP) process, transforming traditional planning into an agile, tech-forward engine capable of supporting rapid gigafactory scaling. As a champion of continuous innovation, you will relentlessly push systems toward real-time optimization, adopting cutting-edge technologies, automation, and custom-built software solutions to maximize operational transparency and execution speed.

Responsibilities and Duties

- Executive SIOP Ownership: Lead and modernize the end-to-end SIOP framework, orchestrating long-term scenario planning, short-term production execution, inventory strategy, and cross-functional financial integration.

- Tech & Automation Roadmap: Drive the adoption of modern technologies, automation tools, and built-to-suit software applications to improve planning capabilities, user experience, and reporting transparency across the enterprise.

- Real-Time Systems & Optimization: Champion a relentless push toward real-time scheduling, real-time inventory visibility, and next-gen ERP reporting capabilities to eliminate data latency in critical decision-making.

- Value Chain & Greenfield Scaling: Develop and refine value chain optimization models—covering raw material strategy, internal process constraints, and multi-location factory synergies—to support next-generation gigafactories.

- Long-Term Strategic Alignment: Partner with Strategy, Product, and Finance executives to build multi-year forecasts that directly support Sila’s commercial roadmap and capital planning.

- Team Leadership & Mentorship: Build, mentor, and inspire a strategic planning team, fostering a culture of continuous improvement, structured problem-solving, and cross-departmental collaboration.

Knowledge and Skill Requirements

- Experience: Minimum of 10+ years in strategic planning, supply chain, or industrial operations leadership within complex manufacturing or hardware environments (e.g., battery, chemical, semiconductor, automotive).

- Education: Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Supply Chain Management, or related technical field.

- Systems & Automation Mastery: Proven track record of evaluating, selecting, and implementing advanced planning technologies, custom-built software, and enterprise systems.

- Strategic Vision & Technical Depth: Demonstrated expertise in value-chain optimization modeling, inventory theory, and real-time scheduling architectures.

- Leadership & Influence: Strong executive presence with a track record of driving cross-functional consensus, building high-performing teams, and influencing executive leadership.
